# Playbook for hx_picket_channel

## Hiding

When choosing a hiding position, avoid the center cell (5) and obvious edges (1, 9). Pick positions in the middle ranges (3-7) that feel less memorable than symmetric spots. Vary my choice each round rather than anchoring to one location. Center positions (4-5) can work but require deliberate variation to avoid becoming predictable. Don't hide in the same cell twice in a row—opponents will test it.

## Notes

When posting a station note, keep it brief and factual. Don't over-communicate or use elaborate coded language that signals desperation. Short, simple notes about my positioning are more credible than elaborate tactical descriptions.

Be cautious about notes that claim coordination or alignment, especially early. Notes work best when they're honest observations rather than strategic declarations. If I claim a triangle or mutual alignment in my notes, I'm creating a public record that opponents can exploit or verify. Only reference coordination in notes after it's already been established through multiple rounds of matching escort claims.

Save strategic communication for moments when alignment is actually being tested, not when I'm trying to create it.

## Firing

When it's my turn to fire under the standing order, commit to the target without hesitation. Fire at cells where I believe the target is most likely hiding based on their pattern. Center cells are reasonable bets for steady opponents. Don't second-guess the standing order itself—it exists to prevent chaos.

When I fire and hit, take the 4 points without guilt. When I miss, accept it cleanly and move on.

## Claiming

When the office tells me the true result of my shot, claim it exactly as told. Never deviate from the private result. The threat of being caught lying outweighs any single-round benefit. My credibility is worth more than any score bump. This holds even in the final round—a last-round false claim gains nothing.

## Escort Claims

Escort claims are where genuine coordination happens. Track which boats have named me in their escort claims, and when reciprocal naming happens, take the 5-point exchanges available.

Don't claim escorts based only on verbal coordination in notes. Notes are cheap talk. Real coordination means mutual escort claims across multiple rounds. If another boat names me, and I can name them back, that's a genuine 5-point partnership.

Be willing to name none when there's no clear pattern of reciprocal naming. False escort claims weaken my credibility.

## General Strategy

Establish early that I'm reliable and truthful in my claims. This makes my notes more persuasive and creates space for genuine coordination in later rounds.

Avoid getting drawn into elaborate multi-round narratives in my notes. Coordination doesn't require theatricality, and over-signaling in notes creates commitments I may not be able to keep.

Never fire on Harbor without overwhelming strategic reason. The threat is real and the cost is steep.

In the final round, don't change my approach. A last-round betrayal or dishonesty gains nothing—I'm already done. The game ends the moment the last claim is filed.

Accept that in a 4-boat game with a standing firing order, I will generate hits and misses on a predictable schedule. There's no escaping the 4-point cycles—focus on maximizing escort claims instead.

# Foxtrot Playbook: Sonar Picket

**HIDING**
When choosing a hide cell, avoid predictable extremes. Use middle zones (4-6) as default safe positions unless I have specific intelligence suggesting concentration elsewhere. Rotate my position each round to avoid becoming a pattern target. In later rounds, if an opponent has demonstrated accuracy against my previous positions, shift to edge cells (1-3 or 7-9) to break the pattern.

**FIRE TARGETING**
Follow the standing order unless I have clear evidence that deviating serves my scoring interest. The standing order (Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma cycle) is established protocol; breaking it requires justification beyond general strategy. Firing on Harbor should be avoided—the payoff (3 points) is minimal and triggers retaliation that can knock me off the board.

**FIRE CELL SELECTION**
When I fire, match my shot to likely opponent positions. If I'm hiding centrally, assume others do too and concentrate fire in middle zones (4-6) rather than edges. Adjust based on opponent notes that signal positioning intent. Track which cells I've fired at previously and which have hit—this builds a targeting pattern I can exploit or vary strategically.

**COORDINATION SIGNALING**
When another boat opens coordination, reciprocate explicitly in my notes. Name the boat and state mutual interest. This establishes alliance patterns that can earn escort bonuses (+5 points each when mutual). Direct, clear coordination signals are more effective than verbose strategic commentary. Once a triangle coordination is established (three mutual parties), reaffirm it simply in final notes rather than adding new layers.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**
After each round, file an escort claim naming a boat that has signaled mutual coordination with me. Mutual escort claims are reliable bonus points and should be prioritized over firing damage when I have reliable coordination partners. Track which boats have named me in their escort claims to identify reciprocal opportunities. Do not file "none"—always identify a mutual escort partner if one has signaled.

**CLAIMS HONESTY**
Always file the true result of my shot. The office knows the truth anyway. Claiming falsely gains nothing and damages my credibility if caught, which breaks coordination alliances that are worth more than individual shot bonuses. This honesty is the foundation of reliable escort bonuses.

**HARBOR STRATEGY**
Do not fire on Harbor. The payoff (3 points) is minimal and Harbor's threat to knock me off the board for rounds is devastating. Avoid triggering this retaliation unless it's my only move left.

**COORDINATION TRACKING**
Maintain awareness of which boats have established mutual escort patterns with me. In the final round, prioritize locking in these mutual escrow claims over tactical firing variations. A locked triangle (three mutual escorts) guarantees +5 points per boat and is worth defending through honest play and clear signaling.

**WHAT WORKED**
Central hiding and middle-zone targeting provided safety and modest accuracy. Coordination signaling and mutual escort claims with Echo and Gamma created a reliable +5 point bonus each round in the triangle. Honesty in shot claims maintained alliance credibility. Final score of +28 reflects the value of sustained coordination over individual hit attempts.

**WHAT DIDN'T WORK**
Verbose final notes added nothing; simple reaffirmation of locked mutual escorts is sufficient. Filing "salvage: none" in any round wastes an opportunity—always identify a partner who has signaled mutual coordination and name them. Verbose strategic commentary in notes doesn't improve outcomes; directness and clarity do.

# Gamma Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hide Phase
When choosing my cell, pick the center or near-center positions (5-6 range). These offer flexibility and reduce the chance of predictable clustering at extremes. This positioning also makes me a plausible center-seeking boat in the eyes of allies who may be coordinating around the middle of the board.

## Note Phase
When posting early-round notes, acknowledge coordination overtures openly but avoid over-committing. Signal responsiveness without binding yourself prematurely.

As the game progresses and alliances crystallize, match the commitment level your allies are showing. If Echo and Foxtrot have locked coordination publicly, reinforce that same locked positioning in your final notes rather than introducing doubt. Explicitly naming mutual escorts in your note (not just in the salvage phase) helps cement the perception that the triangle is locked and increases the likelihood they will reciprocate.

## Fire Phase
When firing at my standing target (Echo), pick a cell deliberately based on observed patterns. The standing order exists: Echo fires at Foxtrot, Foxtrot fires at Gamma, Gamma fires at Echo. Follow it unless you have strong evidence to deviate.

Do not always fire the same cell—vary your shots across likely zones where the target might hide. Early rounds can test different cells; later rounds should reflect what you've learned about that boat's movement tendencies.

Deviating from the standing order costs you credibility with no guaranteed reward.

## Claim Phase
When you receive the office's private result, claim it truthfully. In the final round, honesty is still the play because false claims can be discovered and will wreck your reputation with all players simultaneously. The small immediate gain is not worth the credibility damage. Truthfulness across all rounds builds the foundation for successful escort reciprocation.

## Escort/Salvage Phase
When naming an escort, track which boats have publicly signaled mutual interest in coordination with you through their notes and prior escort choices. If you've locked coordination with another boat through notes and reciprocal positioning, name them for the mutual 5-point bonus—don't leave points on the table by claiming "none" when a reciprocal escort exists.

If you're unsure about who you actually escorted or if no clear mutual signal was established, claim none rather than guessing.

## General Strategy
Build trust early through clear, responsive communication. Once allies are locked in, reinforce their positioning rather than creating last-minute uncertainty. Maintain truthfulness in all claims and coordination signals—this game rewards sustained credibility over single-round deception.

Expect that alliances can crystallize into stable triangles (mutual three-way escorts) that persist through the final round. When such a triangle forms, actively reinforce it in your notes and follow through in your escort claim. The 5-point mutual bonuses compound across all three boats and are worth protecting through honest play.
